paragraphs.text: 1. THE Gods have not ordained hunger to be our death: even to the well-fed man comes death in varied shape.
paragraphs.original: न वा उ देवाः क्षुधमिद्वधं ददुरुताशितमुप गच्छन्ति मृत्यवः ।
paragraphs.translit: na vā u devāḥ kṣudhamidvadhaṃ dadurutāśitamupa gacchanti mṛtyavaḥ |

paragraphs.text: The riches of the liberal never waste away, while he who will not give finds none to comfort him.
paragraphs.original: उतो रयिः पृणतो नोप दस्यत्युतापृणन्मर्डितारं न विन्दते
paragraphs.translit: uto rayiḥ pṛṇato nopa dasyatyutāpṛṇanmarḍitāraṃ na vindate

paragraphs.text: 2. The man with food in store who, when the needy comes in miserable case begging for bread to eat,
Hardens his heart against him-even when of old he did him service-finds not one to comfort him.
paragraphs.original: स्थिरं मनः कृणुते सेवते पुरोतो चित्स मर्डितारं न विन्दते
paragraphs.translit: sthiraṃ manaḥ kṛṇute sevate puroto citsa marḍitāraṃ na vindate

paragraphs.text: 3. Bounteous is he who gives unto the beggar who comes to him in want of food and feeble.
paragraphs.original: स इद्भोजो यो गृहवे ददात्यन्नकामाय चरते कृशाय ।
paragraphs.translit: sa idbhojo yo gṛhave dadātyannakāmāya carate kṛśāya |

paragraphs.text: Success attends him in the shout of battle. He makes a friend of him in future troubles.
paragraphs.original: अरमस्मै भवति यामहूता उतापरीषु कृणुते सखायम्
paragraphs.translit: aramasmai bhavati yāmahūtā utāparīṣu kṛṇute sakhāyam

paragraphs.text: 4. No friend is he who to his friend and comrade who comes imploring food, will offer nothing.
paragraphs.original: न स सखा यो न ददाति सख्ये सचाभुवे सचमानाय पित्वः ।
paragraphs.translit: na sa sakhā yo na dadāti sakhye sacābhuve sacamānāya pitvaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Let him depart-no home is that to rest in-, and rather seek a stranger to support him.
5. Let the rich satisfy the poor implorer, and bend his eye upon a longer pathway.
Riches come now to one, now to another, and like the wheels of cars are ever rolling.
paragraphs.original: ओ हि वर्तन्ते रथ्येव चक्रान्यमन्यमुप तिष्ठन्त रायः
paragraphs.translit: o hi vartante rathyeva cakrānyamanyamupa tiṣṭhanta rāyaḥ

paragraphs.text: 6. The foolish man wins food with fruitless labour: that food -I speak the truth- shall be his ruin.
paragraphs.original: मोघमन्नं विन्दते अप्रचेताः सत्यं ब्रवीमि वध इत्स तस्य ।
paragraphs.translit: moghamannaṃ vindate apracetāḥ satyaṃ bravīmi vadha itsa tasya |

paragraphs.text: He feeds no trusty friend, no man to love him. All guilt is he who eats with no partaker.
paragraphs.original: नार्यमणं पुष्यति नो सखायं केवलाघो भवति केवलादी
paragraphs.translit: nāryamaṇaṃ puṣyati no sakhāyaṃ kevalāgho bhavati kevalādī

paragraphs.text: 7. The ploughshare ploughing makes the food that feeds us, and with its feet cuts through the path it follows.
paragraphs.original: कृषन्नित्फाल आशितं कृणोति यन्नध्वानमप वृङ्क्ते चरित्रैः ।
paragraphs.translit: kṛṣannitphāla āśitaṃ kṛṇoti yannadhvānamapa vṛṅkte caritraiḥ |

paragraphs.text: Better the speaking than the silent Brahman: the liberal friend out values him who gives not.
8. He with one foot hath far outrun the biped, and the two-footed catches the three-footed.
paragraphs.original: एकपाद्भूयो द्विपदो वि चक्रमे द्विपात्त्रिपादमभ्येति पश्चात् ।
paragraphs.translit: ekapādbhūyo dvipado vi cakrame dvipāttripādamabhyeti paścāt |

paragraphs.text: Four-footed creatures come when bipeds call them, and stand and look where five are met together.
9. The hands are both alike: their labour differs. The yield of sister milch-kine is unequal.
paragraphs.original: समौ चिद्धस्तौ न समं विविष्टः सम्मातरा चिन्न समं दुहाते ।
paragraphs.translit: samau ciddhastau na samaṃ viviṣṭaḥ sammātarā cinna samaṃ duhāte |

paragraphs.text: Twins even differ in their strength and vigour: two, even kinsmen, differ in their bounty.
paragraphs.original: यमयोश्चिन्न समा वीर्याणि ज्ञाती चित्सन्तौ न समं पृणीतः
paragraphs.translit: yamayościnna samā vīryāṇi jñātī citsantau na samaṃ pṛṇītaḥ
